raw_case_text:
A 41-year-old Nepalese male of Aryan origin presented with 3 months history of gradually progressive jaundice, intermittent right upper quadrant pain, and weight loss of 5 kg over a 2-month period. There was no history of cough, fever, hemoptysis or shortness of breath. He had received a BCG vaccine at childhood, but there was no prior history of tuberculosis, or family history of contact.
On examination, patient was deeply icteric with skin scratch marks all over the body. On abdominal examination, he had mild hepatomegaly and a palpable gall bladder. Initial laboratory values revealed a WBC count of 9200/mm3 (90% neutrophils, 10% lymphocytes), haemoglobin 12.7 g/dL, total bilirubin 24.4 mg/dL, conjugated bilirubin18 mg/dL, ALT 96 U/L (normal 5-45 U/L), AST 161 U/L (normal 5-45 U/L), and ALP 593 U/L (normal 42-128 U/L), albumin 3.5 mg/dL and total protein 5.7 mg/dL. His random blood sugar, serum urea and creatinine will within normal limits. A chest X-ray film was normal. Abdominal ultrasound examination revealed an irregular hypoechoic lesion of 3 cm x 4.4 cm in the head and uncinate process of pancreas, and with dilation of entire bile duct system, distended gall bladder with normal pancreatic duct. Contrast enhanced CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass in the pancreatic head and uncinate process of the pancreas. (Figure 1) The gall bladder was distended along with the dilatation of entire biliary tract. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a mass of size 3x2 cm at the head and uncinate process of pancreas with areas of necrosis on cut section, 50 ml of thick pus at the retroduodenal region, dilated distal common bile duct, distended gall bladder and multiple enlarged perichodochal and peripancreatic lymph nodes. The patient underwent pancreatoduodencetomy with intraoperative diagnosis of pancreatic carcinoma. AFB staining of the pus was negative and culture was sterile. However, the histopathology from the pancreatic mass revealed necrotizing granulomatous lesion which was positive for acid fast bacilli. The histopathological picture of the enlarged nodes was of reactive lymphadenitis. (Figure 2) The patient had uneventful postoperative period. After the diagnosis of tuberculosis, antitubercular drugs were started in accordance to DOTS (Directly observed treatment, short-course), and patient is doing well at the follow up after 6 month.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 41-year-old male presenting with progressive jaundice, intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and weight loss for three months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 3-month history of progressively worsening jaundice and intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain, accompanied by an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg over the preceding 2 months. He denied cough, fever, chills, hemoptysis, or shortness of breath.
subjective.past_medical_history: Received BCG vaccination in childhood. Denied prior personal history of tuberculosis or known family contact with tuberculosis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Progressive jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, pruritus with generalized skin excoriations, weight loss. Denies fever, night sweats, cough, hemoptysis, or dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Deeply icteric with generalized skin scratch marks. Abdominal examination revealed mild hepatomegaly and a palpable, distended gallbladder. Remainder of physical examination was unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC count 9,200/mm3 (90% neutrophils, 10% lymphocytes), hemoglobin 12.7 g/dL. Total bilirubin 24.4 mg/dL, conjugated bilirubin 18 mg/dL, ALT 96 U/L (normal 5-45 U/L), AST 161 U/L (normal 5-45 U/L), ALP 593 U/L (normal 42-128 U/L), serum albumin 3.5 mg/dL, total protein 5.7 mg/dL. Random blood glucose, serum urea, and creatinine within normal limits. Chest radiograph was normal. Abdominal ultrasound showed an irregular hypoechoic mass measuring 3 cm x 4.4 cm in the head and uncinate process of the pancreas, dilatation of the entire biliary tree, and a distended gallbladder with a normal pancreatic duct.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a heterogeneous mass in the pancreatic head and uncinate process with biliary tree dilation and gallbladder distension. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a 3 x 2 cm mass in the pancreatic head and uncinate process with cut-surface necrosis, 50 mL of thick retroduodenal pus, dilated distal common bile duct, and multiple enlarged pericholedochal and peripancreatic lymph nodes. Pancreatoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) was performed under an intraoperative suspicion of pancreatic carcinoma. Pus AFB stain was negative and bacterial culture was sterile. Histopathology of enlarged lymph nodes demonstrated reactive lymphadenitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Pancreatic tuberculosis (isolated head and uncinate process tuberculous mass with obstructive jaundice) mimicking pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
Diagnostic confirmation: Histopathological examination of the resected pancreatic mass demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with presence of acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain.
Management and outcome: Uneventful postoperative course. Following confirmation of tuberculosis, standard directly observed therapy short-course (DOTS) antitubercular regimen was initiated. Patient made a complete recovery and was doing well at 6-month follow-up.
